It represents the aspirations of the soul to attain the highest spiritual goal - the realization of its inherent divinity. The term 'kaustubha' is from the same root and is a sacred gem worn by Lord Vishnu. The name inspires one to strive for spiritual growth and to seek the inner gold of wisdom and enlightenment.

He was so named because of his 'kaustav' (knowledge) which helped him make wise decisions and lead his kingdom effectively.

Another reference to Kaustav is that of a Jain sage, also named Kaustubh or Kaustav, who is considered a Tirthankar or a Jina in Jainism.
